about: What every screen, page, widget and native view must take from the selected screen look, read by scripts/check-one-look.mjs on every commit, every deploy and every UI edit an AI makes. A rule is DATA: kind says which reading applies (a declaration's value, a style block, or a line), the patterns say what is refused, says is the words the refusal shows. A file kept apart on purpose is a row in kept, with why; a kept row whose file no longer breaks the rule is itself a finding, so the list cannot rot.

rules.says: A font is taken from the screen look: font-family: var(--font-primary) for text, var(--font-display) for titles and quotes (var(--page-font) / var(--page-display) on server pages), never a face named in place.

A font is taken from the screen look: font-family: var(--font-primary) for text, var(--font-display) for titles and quotes (var(--page-font) / var(--page-display) on server pages), never a face named in place.
A font shorthand takes its face from the screen look too: font: 600 1rem var(--font-primary), never a face named in place.
A font named in DATA is taken from the screen look (var(--font-primary) or var(--font-display)); only the look's own themes name faces.
A native font comes from the look's type scale (Typeface in ios/Shared/Look.swift): never Font.custom, a named UIFont/NSFont, or a serif/rounded/monospaced system design.

No card wears a coloured bar down its left side. Show what matters with the look's own surfaces: a tinted card, a status mark, a count, or the nesting guide beside an open list (ui/show/nesting-guide).

No card wears a coloured bar down its left side. Show what matters with the look's own surfaces: a tinted card, a status mark, a count, or the nesting guide beside an open list (ui/show/nesting-guide).
No card or row wears a coloured bar down its side (here drawn as a ::before/::after strip). Mark it with the look's own surfaces instead.
No native card wears a coloured bar down its side. Mark it with the look's own surfaces (Glass, a status symbol).

A filled button is drawn by the shared button (parts/ui Button, or a server page's .page-action), which wears the look's face: its fill, the highlight line along the top and the shadow under it. Never paint a raw colour onto a button.
A native button style that fills its button draws the look's face with .buttonFace() (ios/Shared/ButtonFace.swift): fill, border, the highlight line along the top and the shadow.

A filled button is the shared Button (parts/ui/show/button), which wears the look's face: its fill, the highlight line along the top and the shadow. A hand-built <button> never paints a raw or accent colour of its own; status tints use the look's status tokens (bg-status-error/10).
A filled button variant wears the look's face: its fill with bg-[image:var(--button-sheen)] and shadow-[var(--button-highlight),var(--button-shadow)], never a bare colour.

A button's face is Tailwind's shadow, shadow-[var(--button-highlight),var(--button-shadow)], never a raw [box-shadow:...]: a focus ring replaces a raw box-shadow, so every autofocused or keyboard-focused button turns flat.

A label keeps the case its words were written in: never text-transform: uppercase, a Tailwind uppercase class, textTransform 'uppercase' or Swift .uppercased()/.textCase(.uppercase) on shown words. Write the label in sentence case and let the look set its size and colour.

No eyebrow: a small line above a heading only restates or labels it. Say it in the heading, or leave it out; a component never offers an eyebrow slot and DATA never carries one.

Values are shown through the shared value view (parts/ui SchemaValueView, which picks a designed view from the value's shape in result-views.json), never as JSON text: no pretty-printed JSON.stringify and no JSON.stringify in shown words. There is no raw-data disclosure; a machine field is not shown.

Initials are drawn only for people and only by the shared person mark (parts/ui/show/display-mark/DisplayMark.tsx), whose shape and colour come from the look. A thing (a tool, a run, a course, a space) shows its picture or icon, never letters in a circle, and no screen styles its own round avatar.

A look that names an accent fills its strong action with exactly that accent: --button-primary-bg is the --accent-primary value itself (Trillion's thread red), never a deeper red, ink or white, and its words (--button-primary-text) are white when white reaches 3 to 1 on it (the bar for bold text, so the strong label is semibold), else black. Destructive actions never fill (destructive-is-never-a-fill) and wear --color-error, a different red, so the two never look alike.
A destructive button is the look's danger colour in its words and edge on a neutral face, never a fill: the only filled button is the strong action, which wears the look's accent.

A step's number-or-tick mark is the shared step mark (parts/ui/show/step-mark StepMark) or, for steps the person ticks, the shared steps checklist; no screen draws its own circle, tick or colour for a step.
A step's number-or-tick mark is the shared step mark (parts/ui/show/step-mark StepMark, its look screen-look/show/step-mark.css); no screen styles its own step circle.
A guide row's done status (tone good) wears the shared step mark (StepMark, state done) and the look's success token; no screen paints its own green dot, circle or tick.

A colour is taken from the screen look: var(--bg-primary), var(--text-primary), var(--border-primary), var(--button-primary-bg), var(--color-success) and the other look variables (a tint is color-mix(in srgb, var(--text-primary) 12%, transparent)), never a hex, rgb(), hsl() or named colour written in place. If this surface truly has no look variable, add a kept row with why.

A font is taken from the screen look: var(--font-primary) for text, var(--font-display) for titles, var(--font-mono) for code, never a face named in place, in a font-family, fontFamily or font shorthand.
A button wears the look's corner: border-radius: var(--radius-control) (var(--radius-pill) for a pill), never a radius written in px, rem or %. If it truly has none, add a kept row with why.

A check, radio or switch takes its corner from the screen look: border-radius: var(--radius-check) (a token of the look, set per look by its checkBorderRadius; var(--radius-pill) for a deliberate circle), never a length typed on one screen.

A check beside text is centred on the text's first line by the shared rule in control-beside-text.css: mark the row data-control-row and set --first-line-size / --first-line-leading on it. Never type a margin offset on the control.

A module makes no random value when it loads: the Worker refuses crypto.randomUUID(), Math.random() and getRandomValues() outside a request, so a new account's deploy breaks at load. Make the id on first use (a function that makes it once and keeps it), never in a top-level const.

A sample colour written inside the words an author reads when a palette entry is not a colour; it is never painted. The sales page itself wears the business's own three colours (--page-bg, --page-ink, --page-accent), not a Trillion look.
The nine record-kind hues (--record-kind-blue .. pink). A kind's colour names the kind, the same in every look, so no look variable carries it; the look owns only the neutral ground they sit on.

The transcript and caption chrome drawn over the video in the full-screen player. The media player part paints that ground dark itself (parts/media-playback), and no look variable is always-dark, so white-over-video cannot follow a light look.
The dark letterbox behind a photo or video in the file carousel. A picture is judged on a dark ground whatever the look, and no look variable is always-dark.

in_page.about: What scripts/visual-check.mjs reads in every view it opens before a deploy (readOffLook): text must be set in a face the look names (the first face of each of faces_from, plus also_faces), no element may wear a bar of bar_min_px or more down its left side only (a left border or an inset shadow from the left edge), and a filled button (buttons) whose fill is a colour of raw_fill_saturation or more must wear the look's button face (its sheen over the fill and its shadow). Never accepted: the deploy stops until it is fixed.

scan.about: The files that draw a surface the person sees as a page, a card, a widget or a workspace screen, and so take every colour, face and corner from the look's variables. A rule with files:"scan" reads these globs (regexes on the repository path) and leaves out the owner. The owner of every look literal is src/workspace/looks.json and parts/screen-look/read-data/*, with the theme files that bind the look to CSS. A page that is not drawn in the look on purpose (the sales page wears the business's own three colours) is a kept row with why, never a glob left out.
